card: This PR introduces assert_true() and assert_false() helper functions to test_framework/util.py and migrates existing assert_equal calls checking boolean literals across 95 test files via a scripted diff. This resolves the verbosity and cognitive overhead of trailing boolean arguments in long test assertions while preserving strict boolean type assertions instead of loose truthiness. The change is an internal test framework cleanup that touches no node runtime logic.
changed_since_previous: The overall approach is unchanged; the branch has been rebased and reordered with preparatory commit cleanups ahead of the scripted diff.
evidence: PR description argues that the new helpers 'reduce cognitive tokens when scanning the code (equals to *what*...?)' while maintaining strict boolean type checks over plain truthy `assert` statements
PR description notes that an earlier attempt to add `assert_true()` was previously dropped from merged PR #31874
problem: Functional tests previously validated boolean outcomes using `assert_equal(expr, True/False)`, which places the expected value at the end of potentially long expressions and creates unnecessary visual clutter. Standard Python `assert expr` is unsuitable because it only evaluates truthiness rather than boolean identity and can be disabled in optimized execution modes.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause a functional test to fail or pass erroneously, with no impact on node binaries or consensus behavior.

scope_notes: The bulk of the diff (+648/-521 across 95 files) is purely mechanical and performed using a scripted-diff regex replacement in commit 757107d7da.
summary: Introduces `assert_true()` and `assert_false()` helper functions to the Python test framework (`test_framework/util.py`) that enforce strict boolean comparison. Migrates existing instances of `assert_equal(..., True)` and `assert_equal(..., False)` across 95 functional test files to use the new helpers.
